admission.contract: A JPEG supplied through the public memory-loading API is accepted and converted into internal JPEG component descriptors even when a component's sampling factor does not evenly divide the frame maximum.
admission.predicate: entry.hit && frame.hit && entry.ctx == frame.ctx && frame.time > entry.time && ((frame.h_max % frame.c0h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c0v != 0) || (frame.img_n > 1 && ((frame.h_max % frame.c1h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c1v != 0))) || (frame.img_n > 2 && ((frame.h_max % frame.c2h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c2v != 0))) || (frame.img_n > 3 && ((frame.h_max % frame.c3h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c3v != 0))))
limitations: This binds the public interface to `stbi_load_from_memory`; other public JPEG entry points are not separately modeled.
The source shows acceptance of parsed sampling factors, but not a distinct 'fractional subsampling' flag.

root.contract: The parsed JPEG frame header establishes a fractional component subsampling relation because at least one component sampling factor does not evenly divide the image-wide maximum sampling factor.
root.predicate: frame.hit && ((frame.h_max % frame.c0h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c0v != 0) || (frame.img_n > 1 && ((frame.h_max % frame.c1h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c1v != 0))) || (frame.img_n > 2 && ((frame.h_max % frame.c2h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c2v != 0))) || (frame.img_n > 3 && ((frame.h_max % frame.c3h != 0) || (frame.v_max % frame.c3v != 0))))
limitations: The issue text does not name a concrete malformed header example; this contract uses the source-derived divisibility condition that makes subsampling ratios fractional.
For 1-component JPEGs this predicate can never hold, so the contract is relevant only to multi-component images.

target.contract: JPEG resampling consumes the fractional subsampling state by truncating the per-component horizontal and vertical scale factors and invoking a resampler on that component.
target.predicate: use.hit && use.jpeg == root.frame.jpeg && use.time > root.frame.time && ((root.frame.h_max % use.comp_h != 0) || (root.frame.v_max % use.comp_v != 0)) && use.hs == root.frame.h_max / use.comp_h && use.vs == root.frame.v_max / use.comp_v && ((use.hs * use.comp_h != root.frame.h_max) || (use.vs * use.comp_v != root.frame.v_max))
limitations: The source clearly shows truncated integer resampling factors reaching the resampler call, but the public issue only says this can lead to 'potential issues' and does not identify the exact failure mode.
This contract does not distinguish which specific resample kernel is selected after truncation.
